alerts.reason: Net sales growth slowed from 12.03% in December to 4.05% in March. Units fell 13.2%, mainly reflecting direct-ship weakness, while average unit price rose 19.9% (A, B, D). At that unit decline, price growth above roughly 9.45% would keep June above the threshold. I forecast the price gain fades past that point in July–September.

Revenue growth slowed from 14.23% in December to 4.02% in March. Earlier pricing actions and mix contributed 14.6 percentage points against a 10.6-point volume drag (A, B). I forecast enough pricing benefit persists to keep June above -5%, then falls to 5.6 points or less in July–September while volume remains weak.

Revenue growth slowed from 12.34% in December to 1.78% in March. ADM had committed to purchasing smaller commodity quantities, and contract liabilities fell from $694 million to $473 million (C, D). These are indirect signs of lower future sales. I forecast June stays above -5% and the smaller quantities weigh enough on July–September revenue to cross.

Reported revenue growth slowed by 6.22 percentage points, from 7.54% in December to 1.32% in March. Another slowdown of that size would put June near -4.90%, leaving little room for further weakening in July–September. Headcount reductions and exit costs in Clean Energy & Fueling provide a secondary operating clue (D).

Net sales went from 6.92% growth in December to a 0.76% decline in March. Lower volume hurt sales, while higher customer prices and premium pricing on one project cushioned the decline (A, D, E). I forecast pricing keeps June above -5%, then provides too little support in July–September to offset continued volume weakness.

Total revenue growth slowed from 6.58% to 2.08%. Subtracting SaaS and license revenue from March totals shows other revenue fell about 9.6%, from $82.2 million to $74.3 million, even as SaaS and license revenue grew 10% (A, B). A further 4.5-point slowdown each quarter would leave June near -2.4% and July–September near -6.9%.

Revenue growth slowed from 33.33% in December to 14.85% in March. Chip volumes were still rising and royalties remained stable (B, D), supporting a June result above -5%. Repeating the 18.48-point slowdown would put June near -3.6%, with a further slowdown of just 1.4 points enough for a July–September crossing.

Revenue growth slowed from 36.70% to 19.42%, and sales of higher-value products drove most of the March increase through higher average prices (A). Another 17-point slowdown would still leave June growth positive. I forecast the benefit from product mix weakens enough for growth to cross -5% in July–September.

Revenue growth slowed from 12.83% in December to 2.58% in March (A), while inventories rose $8.2 million over six months (C). Continued demand in MACOM's three primary markets (B) supports a June result above -5%. I forecast sales weaken more gradually than in March and cross the threshold in July–September.

Total revenue growth slowed from 7.80% to 3.34%. Freight volume fell 1%, while fuel surcharges and core pricing helped raise revenue per car 6% despite a less favorable traffic mix (A, B, D). If growth keeps slowing by roughly 4.45 points per quarter as pricing support fades, June lands near -1.1% and July–September near -5.6%.

Revenue growth slowed from 12.58% to 8.91% (A). Steady Dedicated demand supports a June result above -5% (B). One-Way Truckload and Logistics already faced both unusually scarce freight and stronger price competition (D, E). I forecast those volume and rate pressures deepen enough to produce the July–September crossing.

Shipping revenue growth slowed from 27.54% in December to 9.42% in March, and the vessels performed fewer voyage charters than a year earlier (A, D). I forecast a more gradual slowdown from March. A decline in the growth rate of about eight points per quarter would leave June positive and put July–September below -5%.

March revenue grew only $2.3 million, or 1.04%, even though fuel surcharge revenue rose $4.9 million (E). Revenue per mile fell, and rates per mile affect both freight operations (B, D). I forecast surcharges still cushion June enough to stay above -5%, then weaker freight rates drive the July–September crossing.

March revenue fell only 0.1% because a 7.6% increase in revenue per shipment offset most of the decline in shipments and tonnage (A, B, D). If shipments remain about 7% below the prior year, a yield gain of roughly 2% would put revenue below -5%. I forecast enough yield support survives in June but fades to that level in July–September.
